subject: Perimeter zoning and CAIQ evidence pack for Dedicated/Private deployments
messages:
From: Sarah Lambert <sarah.lambert@acmepay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmepay.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ / perimeter zoning questions for Dedicated/Private

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for taking this on. Our InfoSec team is running a CAIQ and SIG intake for our payments stack integration. They flagged a few items where we need explicit evidence showing how Redwood separates tenant workloads across your deployment modes (hosted, Dedicated, and Private) and what the network perimeter looks like for Dedicated vs Private.

Specifically they asked for:
- A diagram that shows perimeter zones (external edge, DMZ, management plane, customer VPCs) and how traffic flows between them for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- A short table of controls for network ACLs / security groups / NAT & internet egress for Dedicated pools vs Private VPCs.
- Any SOC 2 procedures or attestations that reference network segmentation or privileged access to customer VPCs.

Can you get me a CAIQ-friendly evidence pack (diagrams + controls mapping + captions) by early next week (we're targeting Wed 11/05)? If you have a single archive or drive link that's even better.

Thanks — appreciate it.

—Sarah
Sarah Lambert
Security Programs Manager, Acme Payments

Subject: Re: CAIQ / perimeter zoning questions for Dedicated/Private

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear checklist. We're putting together a CAIQ-friendly pack. I'm attaching a perimeter zones diagram (perimeter_zones_diagram_v2.png) and a short index PDF that maps the diagram elements to CAIQ v4 controls (caiq_evidence_index.pdf).

Quick notes:
- Dedicated: customer workloads run on reserved GPU pools in our dedicated tenant clusters. Each dedicated cluster has isolated management plane endpoints reachable only via our management network and customer-configured VPN or VPC peering. We only accept control-plane connections from a limited set of corporate IPs and require mTLS for customer-managed connections.
- Private (VPC-hosted): customers run an instance of our runtime in their VPC (private control plane). Network egress and ingress are controlled entirely by the customer's routing/NAT configuration; Redwood components run in the customer's subnets unless an optional managed transit is provisioned.

I've looped in Dev for the ACL/security-group mapping (Dev — see Sarah's bullets and the CAIQ items; can you attach the CSV mapping and a short note about default deny rules?). Grace — can you confirm where this sits in our SOC 2 narrative and provide a reference to the procedure / policy doc?

Targeting a consolidated pack tomorrow (Tues) EOD so you have time to review before Wed. If that timeline shifts I'll let you know.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 10:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ / perimeter zoning questions for Dedicated/Private

Thanks Hannah. Attached is the raw mapping CSV (vpc_acls_mapping.csv) that enumerates: subnet CIDR ranges (logical), security group intent (ingress/egress rules), authoritative owner (Redwood infra vs customer), NAT/egress flow (managed vs customer), and whether the entity is in a shared or dedicated control plane.

High-level summary:
- All Dedicated clusters run on a dedicated VPC per customer cluster with VPC-level ACLs that implement default-deny inbound and least-privilege outbound. Control plane reachability is restricted to Redwood operator IPs + the customer's VPN endpoints.
- For Private deployments, we ship a runtime image and optionally a managed transit that connects Redwood updates. The customer controls the internet egress; when managed transit is enabled, egress exits through a small set of Redwood-managed egress NATs (listed in the CSV).
- Security groups: we enforce ephemeral management SGs for operator sessions and require SSH/API access be tied to short-lived certs; no static shared keys for control-plane access.

Known limitations / notes for CAIQ reviewers:
- Audit evidence for egress NAT lists is a generated snapshot; we can produce a time-bound list if the assessor needs a specific date.
- We do not have a single account-level firewall appliance for Dedicated clusters; isolation is achieved via VPC boundaries, route tables, and SG/ACL policy.

See attached: vpc_acls_mapping.csv
Also included: sg-and-nat-summary.txt (human-readable summarization).

—Dev
Dev Patel
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attached is the consolidated CAIQ evidence pack for RDW-4783. Contents: 
- perimeter_zones_diagram_v2.png — labelled diagram showing external edge, DMZ, management plane, Dedicated cluster VPCs, and Private deployment variants. Captions map diagram zones to CAIQ control identifiers.
- caiq_evidence_index.pdf — a one-page matrix that maps diagram elements to CAIQ v4 sections and includes short captions.
- vpc_acls_mapping.csv — detailed ACL/SG mappings and NAT egress lists (as of 2025-11-04 snapshot).
- sg-and-nat-summary.txt — human-readable notes about default-deny posture and ephemeral management SGs.

A couple of clarifications for the assessor:
- Where the CAIQ asks about network-level isolation, point the assessor to the diagram (page 1) and the CSV mapping (sheet: dedicated_clusters). The CSV includes an example rule set for Dedicated cluster control-plane ACLs.
- SOC 2 reference: Grace confirmed the applicable SOC 2 control ID is SYS-NTW-02 (network segmentation & monitoring). Grace — I left the SOC 2 control citation in the index PDF.

Next steps: please confirm receipt and whether the assessor wants a dated snapshot of egress NATs or an expanded change-log export. We're happy to produce either. If you want a recorded walkthrough, Michael can join; he runs infra reliability and can speak to the operational guardrails.

Thanks — happy to tweak anything.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
